chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"The Hajj is for well-known months": Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. So whoever intends to perform Hajj should trim their hair when they see the crescent of Dhu al-Qadah, and whoever intends to perform 'Umrah should trim their hair for a month.

key_terms.أَشْهُرٌ مَعْلُوماتٌ: Well-known months (specifically Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.ذُو اَلْحِجَّةِ: Dhu al-Hijjah (the 12th month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.ذُو اَلْقَعْدَةِ: Dhu al-Qadah (the 11th month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.شَوَّالٌ: Shawwal (the 10th month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.وَفَّرَ شَعْرَهُ: Trimmed their hair (ritual act of cutting hair)

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim trim their hair before performing Hajj or Umrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies the specific duration of the Hajj months by linking the ritual preparation (trimming hair) to the sighting of the Dhu al-Qadah crescent, a practice that underscores the importance of lunar visibility in Shia jurisprudence. It distinguishes the preparatory timeline for Hajj versus 'Umrah, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on precise timing for entering the state of Ihram. This ruling highlights the practical application of Quranic commands regarding the 'known months' for pilgrimage.
